alanine: Small amino acid with just a methyl side chain; one-letter code A
arginine: Positively charged amino acid used to make nitric oxide
asparagine: Amino acid first isolated from asparagus juice
aspartic-acid: Negatively charged amino acid; part of the sweetener aspartame
cysteine: Sulfur-containing amino acid that forms disulfide bridges
glutamic-acid: Its salt is MSG, the source of umami flavour
glutamine: The most abundant amino acid in the blood
glycine: The simplest amino acid, with only a hydrogen side chain
histidine: Essential amino acid with an imidazole ring; precursor of histamine
isoleucine: Branched-chain amino acid, an isomer of another BCAA
leucine: Branched-chain amino acid that triggers muscle growth
lysine: Essential amino acid often low in grains
methionine: Sulfur-containing amino acid that starts nearly every protein
phenylalanine: Amino acid people with PKU must avoid
proline: Amino acid with a ring that makes kinks in proteins, common in collagen
serine: Amino acid with a hydroxyl group, a common phosphorylation site
threonine: Essential amino acid with a hydroxyl group; one-letter code T
tryptophan: Amino acid blamed for post-Thanksgiving sleepiness
tyrosine: Amino acid used to make dopamine and adrenaline
valine: Branched-chain amino acid; one-letter code V
